title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. This is from the 'équation des lacets' notes, the continuation of La Longue Marche. They contain Grothendieck's own derivation of what is now the profinite Grothendieck–Teichmüller group. The group \hat{\mathfrak S}^+_{0,3} is the profinite extension of S_3 by \hat\Pi_{0,3} (the profinite free group on two generators). Grothendieck identifies it with SL(2,Z)^ on the next page. It is generated by an involution \sigma_\infty and an element \rho of order 3, which act on \hat\Pi_{0,3} and permute the loops l_0, l_1, l_\infty. The page relies on \rho(l_0)=l_1 and \sigma_\infty(l_0)=l_1. The goal is to describe all automorphisms u with u(\sigma_\infty)=\sigma_\infty and u(\rho)=g\rho, g \in \hat\Pi_{0,3}, that respect the structure (inertia going to the p-th power, with p a unit).

The procedure, begun on the previous page:
1°) Choose \xi with \xi\rho(\xi)\rho^2(\xi)=1 (A). This is exactly the condition that \xi\rho again has order 3, i.e. \xi is a nonabelian 1-cocycle of Z/3 with values in \hat\Pi_{0,3}. Grothendieck parametrizes the solutions by two cohomology classes: \xi=\lambda\rho(\lambda)^{-1} (coboundary) or \xi=\lambda l_0^{-1}\rho(\lambda)^{-1} (B).
2°) Require \gamma \in \hat Z with \sigma_\infty(\xi)=l_1^\gamma \xi^{-1} l_0^\gamma (C), and p=2\gamma+1 \in \hat Z^*.
3°) (this page) Set h_0=\xi^{-1}l_0^\gamma. Using (C) and \sigma_\infty(l_0)=l_1, one gets h_0\sigma_\infty(h_0)=1. So h_0 is a Z/2-cocycle, and Grothendieck asserts it is a coboundary: h_0=\sigma_\infty(g_0)^{-1}g_0. The diagonal margin note seems to remark that this is evident.
4°) Put g=\sigma_\infty(g_0) l_1^\gamma \rho(g_0)^{-1}. Since \sigma_\infty(g_0)=g_0 l_0^{-\gamma}\xi and \rho(l_0)=l_1, this equals c\,\xi\,\rho(c)^{-1} with c=g_0 l_0^{-\gamma}. Hence g\rho=c(\xi\rho)c^{-1} has order 3 automatically, and u is defined by u(\sigma_\infty)=\sigma_\infty, u(\rho)=g\rho.

Conclusion. The only delicate point (existence and/or uniqueness) is equation (C) in \gamma together with 2\gamma+1 being a unit. This is a condition on \lambda, of two types according to which form (B) is used. Grothendieck predicts, and the next page confirms, that the type is governed by p mod 3: \gamma \equiv 0 or -1 mod 3, never \equiv 1.

Modern dictionary. p=2\gamma+1 is the GT parameter \lambda, and \gamma=m=(\lambda-1)/2. (A)/(B) correspond to the hexagon (order-3) relation, (C) to the 2-cycle relation. Here f need not lie in the commutator subgroup, so this treats a slightly larger group than Drinfeld's \widehat{GT}.
errors: No mathematical errors detected. Step 3 is consistent: h_0\sigma_\infty(h_0)=l_1^{-\gamma}\sigma_\infty(l_0)^\gamma=1, given \sigma_\infty(l_0)=l_1.

Gap: the claim that every Z/2-cocycle h_0 (h_0\sigma_\infty(h_0)=1) is a coboundary is asserted without proof. It is true. \hat\Pi_{0,3}\rtimes\langle\sigma_\infty\rangle is the profinite completion of Z * Z/2, and involutions in a free profinite product are conjugate into a factor (Herfort–Ribes type result). Conjugation by \sigma_\infty fixes \sigma_\infty, so the conjugator can be taken in \hat\Pi_{0,3}. The step is correct but is more than 'évident' in the profinite setting.
The dependence of g on the choice of g_0 (unique up to the centralizer of \sigma_\infty in \hat\Pi_{0,3}) is not discussed.

ideas.what: Viewing the order-3 condition (gρ)^3=1 as a nonabelian Z/3-cocycle equation and parametrizing its solutions by two cohomology classes (λρ(λ)^{-1} and λ l_0^{-1}ρ(λ)^{-1})
ideas.modern_name: nonabelian H^1(Z/3, \hat F_2) / conjugacy classes of order-3 elements in the coset ρ\hat F_2; hexagon relation of GT
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (1990), Ihara (1991) for the hexagon relation; the cohomological parametrization is folklore
ideas.where_published: Not in Esquisse; this is in the unpublished Longue Marche continuation

ideas.what: Two-cycle relation σ_∞(ξ)=l_1^γ ξ^{-1} l_0^γ with p=2γ+1 a unit
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme alludes to the 'Teichmüller tower' and the dimension ≤2 relations, not to these explicit formulas

ideas.what: Triviality of the Z/2-cocycle h_0 (every involution in σ_∞\hatΠ is \hatΠ-conjugate to σ_∞)
ideas.modern_name: conjugacy of finite subgroups in free profinite products

ideas.what: Reconstructing the automorphism u (u(σ_∞)=σ_∞, u(ρ)=gρ) of \hat{\mathfrak S}^+_{0,3} from (λ,γ)
ideas.modern_name: action of \widehat{GT} on \widehat{PSL_2(Z)} / \widehat{SL_2(Z)} (or \hat B_3 mod center)

ideas.what: Which of the two cocycle classes occurs is determined by p mod 3 (γ≡0 or −1 mod 3, never 1)
ideas.modern_name: an elliptic order-3 element goes to a conjugate of ρ^{λ}; λ mod 3 selects the class
ideas.usually_credited_to: implicit in GT literature (e.g. Lochak–Schneps); unsure of explicit statement

missed.claim: Grothendieck formulates the existence/uniqueness of γ in (C), as a condition on λ, as the sole delicate point. He works without assuming f lies in the commutator subgroup, so both classes in (B) are allowed. He predicts a dichotomy by p mod 3, tested on the next page by reduction to SL(2,Z/6Z). An explicit treatment of this 'enlarged GT' with both cocycle classes, and the mod-3 selection rule, is to my knowledge not prominent in the literature, though it is likely implicit.
missed.quote: la seule question délicate, laquelle l'existence (ou l'unicité, ou les deux) d'une solution, est problématique, est l'équation C (en γ∈\hat Z) — plus la condition annexe que 2γ+1 ∈ \hat Z^×
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Papers on automorphisms of profinite braid groups and of \widehat{SL_2(Z)}, and on GT with f not in the derived subgroup, could compare against Grothendieck's direct cohomological parametrization.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful but essentially standard derivation of the GT defining relations (hexagon and 2-cycle) in cocycle language. It is historically interesting as Grothendieck's independent approach, with the two-class parametrization and the p mod 3 dichotomy, but contains no result clearly absent from later work.
transcription_corrections: \hat\pi_{0,3} should be \hat\Pi_{0,3} throughout (capital Pi, as on the neighbouring pages).
'l'existence [-donc-] l'unicité, ou les deux)' should read 'l'existence (ou l'unicité, ou les deux)'.

The struck word before 'laquelle' is 'pour' (struck); the sentence reads 'Ici, la seule question délicate, laquelle l'existence (ou l'unicité, ou les deux) d'une solution, est problématique, est l'équation C'.
The last line reads 'Je prévois qu'on est dans l'une ou', continued on the next page as 'l'une ou l'autre des formules (B)'.

The diagonal margin note is only partially legible. A plausible reading: 'NB j'ai omis [?] le fait que l'existence de γ satisfaisant (C) ... équivaut à ... h_0σ_∞(h_0)=1 ... i.e. ξ = l_0^γ h_0^{-1} ... et unicité ... (A)⇒(A) ... évident!'. It appears to comment on the Z/2-cocycle step and its equivalence with (C).
